units.source_text: 他们如此出走，消息势必传出。

en.t: Since they had fled in this way, word of it was bound to get out.

units.source_text: 大夫监素性倔强，闻知了定将追赶。

en.t: The Senior Secretary was stubborn by nature, and once he heard of it, he would surely come after them.

units.source_text: 他们生怕遭逢此厄，雇的是一艘快船，上有特殊装置。

en.t: Fearing that disaster, they had hired a fast boat fitted with special equipment.

units.source_text: 幸而又值顺风，便不顾危险，飞速开向京都去了。

en.t: Fortunately, they also had a favorable wind, so they ignored the danger and sped toward the capital.

units.source_text: 路中有一处名叫响滩，波涛十分险恶，幸而平安驶过。

en.t: Along the way there was a place called Hibiki-nada, where the waves were extremely treacherous, but luckily they passed through safely.

units.source_text: 路上有人看见这船，相与言道：“这怕是海盗的船了。

en.t: People along the route saw the boat and said to one another, "That must be a pirate boat.

units.source_text: 这么小的船，却像飞一般行走。”

en.t: It is such a small boat, yet it moves as if it were flying."

units.source_text: 被人比作贪财的海盗倒不可怕，可怕的倒是那个凶狠的大夫监的追赶。

en.t: Being taken for greedy pirates was not frightening; what truly frightened them was pursuit by that fierce Senior Secretary.
Everyone in the boat was sick with anxiety.

units.source_text: 玉鬘经过响滩时吟诗道：

en.t: As Tamakazura passed Hibiki-nada, she composed a poem:
